newsitem.title: USA: Gun leads to panic around N.C. race-killing court.
newsitem.headline: Gun leads to panic around N.C. race-killing court.

text.p: Police cordoned off the streets surrounding a North Carolina courthouse Tuesday while they hunted for an armed man who was initially feared to have a connection to a race killings trial going on inside.
The eight-block stretch of downtown Wilmington was closed for a short time Tuesday morning until police determined there was no threat of any violence

Inside the New Hanover County Courthouse, a jury was listening to attorneys argue over whether Malcolm Wright, a former U.S. Army paratrooper, should be put to death for the shooting deaths of a black couple in Fayetteville, N.C., in December 1995.
Wright, 23, who is white, was convicted Friday of slaying Jackie Burden and Michael James as part of an initiation ritual for a white supremacist group at Fort Bragg.

A spokesman for the county sheriff's department said the armed man went to the courthouse to retrieve an assault rifle taken from him when he was picked up on a routine warrant. He said someone called police because the man, whose gun was legal, seemed nervous.

"There was no danger," the spokesman said, although the search sent bystanders around the courthouse into a panic and prompted rumours including one that the unidentified man, who was wearing an olive-drab suit, was wearing military fatigues.
The spokesman said the man had left the scene and police had lifted the barricades by midday.
